rationale: K4 (M60 kotlin deep review, 2026-09-27): the `contains` classes and every ownership boundary that SUPPRESSES one. All four analyzer defects this class found PUBLISHED a new edge, so a fixture pinning only emissions would have missed every one of them — the forbids are the load-bearing half. The through-line: a thing is a member of a class exactly when it is DECLARED IN THAT CLASS'S BODY. The walk threads an owner through every node it does not intercept, and that one fact produced four defects: an init-block local owned by its class (aa6a2beb), a local function, a local class, and — as a consequence of the owner flattening being RIGHT — a data-class componentN count that then over-generated. Two things here are pinned because NO corpus can pin them. The Compose UI-tree rule has zero coverage: neither Exposed nor kotlinx-coroutines contains a single @Composable file, so that rule is load-bearing by fixture ALONE. The data-class componentN count is likewise only visible in a file with a data class AND a companion object — the combination that produced component8 and component9 on a 7-property class — so `Seven` plus `Generated` assert an exact count rather than a lower bound. Naming note, because it cost a run: the helper was first written `anonries` and the expectations spelled it `anonries` — one transposed pair. The runner reported three `expected relationship not found` rows that read exactly like three missing edges, and the analyzer was right and the fixture wrong. An authored expectation whose `from` is a near-miss for a real symbol is indistinguishable from a missing edge until somebody reads the source, so the name is now `anonymousForms` and no longer sits one transposition away from a plausible misspelling. `WithCompanion2` exists because `Seven`'s component8/9 forbids are NOT independently load-bearing: reverting the fix on a data class with no companion and no body properties leaves the count unchanged, so those rows document the production shape (Exposed's ColumnDiff) while `BodyProperty->component2` is the row that actually goes red. Without a companion in the fixture, the real defect has no executable check here at all.

THE production defect, in the shape it occurred: with a companion present, counting every owned property instead of the primary-constructor ones publishes component3 and component4 for a 2-property data class. Kotlin generates component1..component2 and nothing else. Exposed's ColumnDiff published component1..component9 for 7 properties
